legend: The problem was inspired by Pied Piper story. After a challenge from Hooli's compression competitor Nucleus, Richard pulled an all-nighter to invent a new approach to compression: middle-out.
You are given two strings %%ZSMJ0%% and %%ZSMJ1%% of the same length %%ZSMJ2%%. Their characters are numbered from %%ZSMJ3%% to %%ZSMJ4%% from left to right (i.e. from the beginning to the end).
In a single move you can do the following sequence of actions:
move the %%ZSMJ7%%-th character of %%ZSMJ8%% from its position to the beginning of the string or move the %%ZSMJ9%%-th character of %%ZSMJ10%% from its position to the end of the string.
Note, that the moves don't change the length of the string %%ZSMJ11%%. You can apply a move only to the string %%ZSMJ12%%.
For example, if %%ZSMJ13%%"test" in one move you can obtain:
if %%ZSMJ14%% and you move to the beginning, then the result is "test" (the string doesn't change),
if %%ZSMJ15%% and you move to the beginning, then the result is "etst",
if %%ZSMJ16%% and you move to the beginning, then the result is "stet",
if %%ZSMJ17%% and you move to the beginning, then the result is "ttes",
if %%ZSMJ18%% and you move to the end, then the result is "estt",
if %%ZSMJ19%% and you move to the end, then the result is "tste",
if %%ZSMJ20%% and you move to the end, then the result is "tets",
if %%ZSMJ21%% and you move to the end, then the result is "test" (the string doesn't change).
You want to make the string %%ZSMJ22%% equal to the string %%ZSMJ23%%. What is the minimum number of moves you need? If it is impossible to transform %%ZSMJ24%% to %%ZSMJ25%%, print -1.
input: The first line contains integer %%ZSMJ26%% (%%ZSMJ27%%) — the number of independent test cases in the input.

Each test case is given in three lines. The first line of a test case contains %%ZSMJ28%% (%%ZSMJ29%%) — the length of the strings %%ZSMJ30%% and %%ZSMJ31%%. The second line contains %%ZSMJ32%%, the third line contains %%ZSMJ33%%. Both strings %%ZSMJ34%% and %%ZSMJ35%% have length %%ZSMJ36%% and contain only lowercase Latin letters.
There are no constraints on the sum of %%ZSMJ37%% in the test (i.e. the input with %%ZSMJ38%% and all %%ZSMJ39%% is allowed).
output: For every test print minimum possible number of moves, which are needed to transform %%ZSMJ40%% into %%ZSMJ41%%, or -1, if it is impossible to do.
